name: Motivational interviewing
description: Inspired by the spirit and core skills of MI (partnership, acceptance, compassion, evocation; OARS). Our own wording — not the MITI coding manual.

scale.meaning: 1 = not present in this session, 3 = partly present, 5 = strongly and skilfully present

dimensions.label: Evoking the client's own reasons
dimensions.description: Drawing out the client's own desire, ability, reasons and need for change, and responding to change talk when it appears.

anchors.1: Change talk goes unnoticed, or the therapist supplies the reasons for change.
anchors.3: Some change talk is noticed and reflected.
anchors.5: Change talk is consistently drawn out, reflected and strengthened.

dimensions.label: Partnership
dimensions.description: Treating the client as the expert on their own life; working alongside rather than in charge.

anchors.1: The therapist positions themselves as the expert directing the client.
anchors.3: Some collaboration, with moments of directing.
anchors.5: A genuine partnership throughout; the client's expertise is respected.

dimensions.label: Resisting the urge to fix
dimensions.description: Holding back from persuading, advising without permission or arguing for change.

anchors.1: Frequent persuasion, unsolicited advice or arguing with sustain talk.
anchors.5: No persuasion; information or advice is offered only with permission.

dimensions.label: Supporting autonomy
dimensions.description: Explicitly affirming the client's right and capacity to choose.

anchors.1: Choices are made for the client.
anchors.5: Choice and control are clearly left with the client.

dimensions.label: Depth of reflections
dimensions.description: Using complex reflections (meaning, feeling, double-sided) rather than only repeating content.

anchors.5: Frequent complex reflections, including double-sided reflections of ambivalence.

dimensions.label: Working with ambivalence
dimensions.description: Exploring both sides of ambivalence with curiosity rather than pushing one side.

anchors.1: Ambivalence is argued with or ignored.
anchors.3: Ambivalence is named but not explored.
anchors.5: Both sides are explored with curiosity, helping the client hear their own mixed feelings.
